newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan bourse blue chip options rise to 18 in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Milan bourse blue chip options rise to 18 in Jan.

text.p: Six more Italian blue chip share options will be traded from January 20 bringing the total to 18, the bourse regulatory authority Consob said.
At the same time, trading of "premi" contracts on shares for which standard options are also traded will no longer be permitted on the screen-based market, a Consob statement said.

Premi contracts, or traditional options, can be based on shares, convertible bonds, warrants and rights subscriptions traded on the Milan stock market. They are traded according to the traditional types - dont (call), put, stellage, strap and strips. Options trading involves just puts and calls.
Trading in six blue chip share options began on the new IDEM derivatives market in February. The number rose to 12 in September.
The newcomers are Pirelli ordinary, Olivetti ord, Mediobanca ord, Gemina ord, Stet savings and Telecom Italia savings .

Trading in premi contracts which have underlying stocks other than those of the options market will not be affected and operators will still be allowed to trade premi contracts based on IDEM shares off-market or in a future separately organised market.
Premi contracts, previously traded in an open outcry market, were transferred to a computerised system in February this year just before the trading in the original six stock options began.
The aim of the transfer was to increase the degree of transparency in the price formation process in the relatively illiquid market and to improve its depth.

But a debate among market operators and the regulatory authorities emerged on whether to permit trading of premi contracts on the most highly capitalised shares for which standard options were also traded, given the possibility that the coexistence of both types of contracts might segment liquidity.

Consob said the prohibition of the premi trading alongside options was in line with market sentiment ahead of privatisation of the stock exchange and justified by the wish to concentrate liquidity in the market considered likely to be more efficient.

The 12 blue chip shares in which options have been traded so far are the ordinary shares of Mediaset, INA, IMI, Banca Commerciale Italiana, Montedison, Edison, Generali, Fiat, ENI, Telecom Italia, TIM and Stet.
